intent: A medical historian telling it as a story: the village and the boy, the test that could have killed him, then the long line from one hand to a disease wiped off the planet.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which country gave the world its FIRST vaccine?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which country gave the world its first vaccine?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: England. Edward Jenner, a country doctor in Berkeley, gave the very first on 14 May 1796.

lines.direction: push in on the Severn and Berkeley's pin; the cow sticker on 'scratched', the syringe on 'arm'; on 'vacca' a LATIN / ENGLISH split — VACCA, Latin for cow, against VACCINE, the word he coined
lines.text: He scratched cowpox from a milkmaid's hand into the arm of 8-year-old James Phipps. Vacca is Latin for cow.

lines.direction: ease out a little; the hourglass on 'weeks'; on 'nothing' the shield sticker and a relieved flag-ball; on 'killed' the 3 IN 10 card and the skull sticker — this is the stake, said plainly
lines.text: Weeks later he exposed the boy to smallpox and nothing happened to him. Smallpox killed 3 in every 10.

lines.direction: pull back over the Channel; a line draws from Berkeley to Geneva with the syringe travelling along it; the Geneva pin and tag; the globe sticker on 'only'
lines.text: In 1980 the WHO in Geneva declared smallpox eradicated, still the only human disease ever wiped out.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
